subject: Recap: Security requirements & next steps (FinPay)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Security requirements & next steps (FinPay)

Alex — thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can align with your security and procurement teams. Recreating the high-level notes here so your legal/security folks can skim.

Key pain points you called out:
- SOC 2 Type II evidence and gap confirmation (audit scope, date)
- Audit log capture and export (schema, retention, SIEM integration)
- DPA terms and data residency (EU/US controls, subprocessors)
- Pen test evidence and remediation summary (redacted findings)
- Retention policy: current expectation ~90 days but regulator ask could push to 1 year

Project goals we heard:
- Proof that Redwood can meet SOC/DPA commitments for production inference by Q3
- Exportable, structured audit logs for transaction-level tracing into your SIEM
- Clear retention settings per environment (prod vs non-prod) and a default purge policy

What Redwood will deliver (owners & target dates):
1) Redacted SOC 2 report & controls summary (Marissa) — by 2026-03-05 (PDF stub attached)
2) Pen-test high-level summary + remediation status (Neha) — by 2026-03-05 (redacted)
3) Draft Data Processing Addendum (Marissa) — by 2026-03-05 (DOCX attached)
4) Audit-log schema example and sample payloads (Neha) — same day (JSON attached)
5) Architecture diagram showing data flows and where logs are emitted (Neha) — share link to Drive
6) Schedule 45–60 min technical review with your security + infra teams (Marissa) — proposed times below

Proposed times for technical review (PT):
- Wed 2026-03-04 10:00–11:00
- Thu 2026-03-05 14:00–15:00
Please pick one or suggest alternatives and include legal/security contacts.

Attachments (stubs included):
- SOC2-summary-redacted.pdf (redacted, control matrix + audit date)
- audit-log-schema-example.json (example events & field definitions)
- DPA-draft-redwood.docx (editable draft for your counsel)

Open questions for you to confirm in reply:
- Do you require full raw pen-test reports or will a redacted exec summary + remediation log suffice for initial procurement?
- Desired retention default: confirm 90 days vs 365 days for production logs
- Any specific subprocessors / KMS requirements we should map in the DPA?

Thanks — I’ll get the listed artifacts into your inbox by EOD Friday, and Neha will lead the technical review.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@finpay.com>

Cc: Priya Agarwal <priya.agarwal@finpay.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Security requirements & next steps (FinPay)

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A few quick notes from our side after internal sync: 

1) Please include our legal contact (Priya Agarwal) on the DPA thread — Priya is copied.
2) For procurement: an exec-summary of the pen test + remediation timeline is acceptable to start, but our infosec team will require the full report under NDA before production onboarding. Can you confirm Redwood has a standard NDA process for that exchange?
3) Retention: we are likely to ask for 1 year retention for audit logs in production; 90 days is OK for non-prod. Please indicate any additional storage/cost implications if we request 365 days.
4) Audit export: we use Splunk; confirm you can push logs to our HTTP Event Collector / S3 bucket (we prefer S3 + KMS).

We are available for the technical review on Thu 2026-03-05 14:00 PT.

Attaching: vendor-security-questionnaire.xlsx (initial answers populated) — please review and tell us any fields you want Redwood to fill or own.

Alex
Alex Mercer
Head of Security Engineering, FinPay
